svg.text: Every prime of the σ₁ / moonshine analysis, drawn once — Ogg (supersingular) primes at the core, new primes on outer shells.
105 distinct primes, each drawn once; repeated primes are referenced by dots, and repunits (“just ones in base N”) wear a cyan halo.
all ones in some base (see lenses)
The core is the 15 Ogg primes,
the centre out to the nine
exponent-1 primes on the gold ring.
No prime is drawn twice. A prime
that recurs on an outer shell keeps
its innermost home and gets one
A cyan halo flags a prime that is
a string of ones in some base —
p-adic lenses — the same primes as “just ones”
A prime with a cyan halo is a base-b repunit: 1 + b + … + bᵏ⁻¹ = a run of k ones. Each lens views the flagged primes in one base (optimal = smallest base, most ones).
15 of the 105 primes are repunits — a string of ≥3 ones in some base. Two are repunits in two bases: 31 = 11111₂ = 111₅, 8191 = 1…1₂ (13) = 111₀₅ (☉ marks them).
σ₁(pᵉ) = 1 + p + … + pᵉ is itself a base-p repunit; the primes above are the members of the series that are repunits in their own right.
Every prime and every repunit flag is machine-checked in Lean 4 / Mathlib (RequestProject/RepunitPrimes.lean) — no sorry, standard axioms only.
